chapter: Technique and life on the road (repeated passages)
title: Good lead trombonists he knew, including Dan Minor and Dickie Wells
summary: He declines to name the best lead trombonist but recalls Dan Minor, Dickie Wells and Henry Coker.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Who was the best lead trombonist here in Washington.
Oh, that would be hard to say. That would really be hard to say. I don't know. I don't want to do anybody any injustice. That's why I wouldn't say.
Well there's been some very good ones. Some very good ones. And off hand it's hard for me to recall them all you know.
Because I imagine some of them might not be so well known because they often aren't soloists. At least not what you might call ________ soloists.
Yeah a lot of them, yeah.

You see that's the thing -- I can't remember names. I wish I could. In the band with Basie we had a good trombone player, Stan Minor. He's not heard of much. No one ever heard of him but he was with Basie when I was, and Dickie Wells (PHONETIC). And Dickie Wells (PHONETIC) played a lot of lead too and that was beautiful too. He was beautiful lead trombone.

Henry Koger (PHONETIC), and oh gee, I can't name them. You know. And as far as records is concerned, then you have to go to another bag because I don't remember who all I played with in records. And there was so many great trombone -- straight lead men you know.
